verdict.rationale: Vercel documents running server-side code (Fluid compute functions, and middleware-style code that runs before a request completes) and lets developers choose which regions functions run in, per project or per function, with failover regions on Enterprise. This places compute closer to users by explicit regional choice. However, the default is a single region (iad1), and no evidence shows code running automatically across a global edge network; the 'close to your users' CDN language covers cached files and images, not code. Missing for 10: documented global edge execution of code, evidence of a multi-location edge runtime, and independent corroboration of low-latency execution near users.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run my code on a global edge network close to end users

citations.quote: You can override regions for individual functions using the functions property in your project configuration.
Enterprise users can also use functionFailoverRegions to specify regions that a Vercel Function should failover to if the default region is out of service.
Run code before a request completes to rewrite, redirect, or personalize responses.
Run server-side code on demand with Fluid compute, which scales concurrency for AI and I/O-heavy workloads.
